messages:
Alex (SRE): heads-up — getting a cluster alert storm in eu-west2 since ~10:23 UTC. controller-manager leader changes every ~30s and apiserver 5xx for watch requests. CPU fine but watch latency skyrockets.
Maria (Oncall): saw it too, alerting on 5xx p50->p95 jump. KVstore compaction latency spiked around the same time.
Cheng (Provisioner): provisioning queue for Dedicated GPU pools jumped, saw many AttachTimeouts back-to-back. suspecting attach path is blocked, not GPU scheduler itself.
Kai (Infra): any NAT/egress saturation? eu-west2 SNAT metrics look noisy but conntrack counts are normal. Could be asymmetric path causing kubelet -> controlplane packet loss.
Alex (SRE): paste of apiserver logs: 
```
E1012 10:24:12.345 apiserver.go:123] failed to serve watch: timeout writing response: write tcp 10.0.3.12:6443->10.1.4.9:53324: i/o timeout
E1012 10:24:13.678 etcdclient.go:89] kvstore compaction took 1.9s (threshold 500ms)
```
Maria (Oncall): deploy-bot shows a kube-proxy canary rolled 10:20 and then reverted 10:28 in eu-west2. could be related. :thinking:
deploy-bot: Canary rollback triggered for kube-proxy in eu-west2 at 10:28:02 UTC (reason: increased watch latency).
Cheng (Provisioner): dug into provisioner logs: attach-controller kept retrying mounts due to ECONNRESET to the storage apiserver in the same subnet. restarting kube-proxy cleared some of the stray conn resets.
Lina (Platform): controller-manager leader lock bounced because lease update failed intermittently. that explains flapping, leader-election timeouts cause reconcilers to pile up -> more apiserver watch pressure.
Kai (Infra): I see a handful of nodes with kernel conntrack entries expiring aggressively; iptables connmark churn from the kube-proxy regression caused a short window of packet drops. restarting kube-proxy on ~12 nodes reduced drop rate.
Alex (SRE): action taken: rolled back kube-proxy to previous image across eu-west2, restarted controller-manager pods where leader-election stuck, and cordoned one noisy node. saw leader hold for ~1m now.
Cheng (Provisioner): attach queue length dropped from 120 -> 20 after kube-proxy rollback, but GPU attach error rate still at ~2%. continuing to drain and reprovision a few nodes.
Maria (Oncall): mitigation: moved low-priority inference traffic off eu-west2 routing using smart-routing (temporary), scaled down a couple Dedicated pools to reduce attach churn.
Lina (Platform): note for follow-up: consider leader-election tuning and backoff for controller-manager leader renewals; and add a canary e2e watch test on kube-proxy changes.
Kai (Infra): cost note: autoscaler overprovisioned some spare GPUs during churn; we should tag the surge as emergency and reconcile billing alerts. linking metric dashboard: https://grafana.internal/r/cluster-eu-west2
Alex (SRE): current status: controller-manager leader stable, apiserver watch 5xx reduced to baseline but still monitoring. keeping the rollback for 30m then decide on patch.
Cheng (Provisioner): I'll run a deeper replay of attach-controller traces and collect journalctl for nodes that had mount resets. opening a follow-up ticket.
Maria (Oncall): will keep monitoring for 20m; if watch 5xx > 5% for 5m we escalate to SEV. tagging Cheng for postmortem. :+1:
Alex (SRE): thanks all — creating incident doc and assigning follow-up steps (Cheng: provisioner traces, Lina: leader-election tuning proposal, Kai: conntrack/iptables postmortem).
